## Capturing Meeting Content

:::{.callout-tip icon="false" collapse="false"}
### {{< fa brain >}} Learning Objectives

After completing this topic you will be able to: 

<u>Paraphrase</u> why recording meeting content 'as you go' is useful

:::
 
As you go, and definitely before your meeting is over, engage your team in synthesizing and capturing the information that has been discussed. This helps you to deepen understanding, document your workflow and decisions, and pick up easily next time. Use a consistent system - like a running notes document linked in the calendar item. Graphics or drawings can be a valuable complement to oral and written content in making thinking visible.

<p align="center">
<img src="topics/images/image_visible-thinking.png" alt="Art of many groups of people with blue speech bubbles connected by an orange amorphous cloud" width="100%"/>
<figcaption> Making thinking visible, Credit: Nancy Margulies, World Cafe, Flickr </figcaption>
</p>

Consider using:

- Grids to organize information
- Conceptual models or mind maps to articulate shared understanding of complex systems 
- Project briefs, abstracts, and other written collateral to distill ideas

When capturing notes, try to use people's own words; if necessary ask them to distill long or complex points into a headline you can capture. Invite them to offer corrections if the notetaker didn't capture what they meant.

::::{.callout-warning icon="false"}
### {{<fa rocket >}} Activity: Team Planning

:::{.panel-tabset}
### Part 1 - Reflection

On your own, think about your upcoming first team meeting:

- What do you think should be the purpose of this first meeting? What would you like to accomplish?
- What do you think your group _must_ do or discuss in order to launch your work together well?

### Part 2 - Team Discussion

In your project teams

- Identify a facilitator, timekeeper, scribe/notetaker, and reporter for today’s breakout session (not the meeting)
- Use round robin or silent Google Doc-ing to hear everyone’s answers to the prompts. Don’t discuss or edit until you have heard from everyone:
-- What do you see as the overarching purpose of our first team meeting?
-- What’s one thing that we must accomplish (i.e. one intended outcome)?

- Discuss and refine the plan for your meeting together:
  - Agree on the meeting purpose
  - Identify 1-3 intended outcomes
  - Decide on meeting length
  - Draft an agenda for the meeting

- Discuss: What activities or facilitation techniques will you use to move through this agenda? How will you ensure inclusive and equitable participation? 

- Discuss: Based on your previous experience, how might things get off track? What’s your plan if they do?
 
- Identify roles and responsibilities
  - Facilitator:
  - Timekeeper:
  - Notetaker / Scribe:

- Identify any prep work for participants and for the facilitator(s)

- Calendar the meeting, if time permits!


### Part 3 - Class Share-out

Report out:

- What did you identify as your purpose and intended outcomes?
- What activities or facilitation practices did you identify to help make your meeting inclusive and effective?
